newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ZEMAN SIGNS ONE-YEAR CONTRACT WITH ROMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZEMAN SIGNS ONE-YEAR CONTRACT WITH ROMA.

text.p: Czech coach Zdenek Zeman, sacked earlier this year by Italian serie A side Lazio, will take charge of city rivals Roma next season in a surprise move which shocked both players and supporters.

Stop-gap trainer Nils Liedholm announced the coup, which will bring Zeman back to Rome's Olympic Stadium -- the ground the two teams share -- under an agreement that could enrage Lazio fans still smarting from his sacking in January.
With former Roma coach Sven Goran Eriksson set to coach Lazio next season, future Roma-Lazio derbies could prove a surreal experience for the city's soccer fans.
"Zeman is the right choice for Roma. It was not a rushed decision. We were after him for days," the 74-year-old Liedholm told reporters after meeting club president Franco Sensi.
"We were able to get him when it didn't seem possible. I like him. He's an attacking trainer like me."
Zeman, whose one-year contract is worth a reported 1.5 billion lire ($880,000), said he was delighted.
"I am happy with the trust shown in me. It's a position I accept with great satisfaction. I'm pleased to be staying in Rome," he said.
Lazio sacked Zeman in January this year after a poor start to the season, replacing him with club president and former Italy goalkeeper Dino Zoff as a stop-gap.
Zeman's move is likely to annoy fans who stayed loyal to the Czech after the sacking, greeting him with cheers when he took his seat at the first home game he attended as a spectator.
He had been coach at Lazio since 1993, enjoying good results and taking the club to second place in the league in 1994-95 and third the following season.
Some Lazio players greeted the signing with disbelief. "I can't believe it," Lazio midfielder and fellow Czech Pavel Nedved said of the move. Zoff refused to be drawn on the issue.
"I don't comment on other people's affairs," he said.
Tuesday's move made Zeman the fifth coach to work for both Rome clubs. Sampdoria's Eriksson, who took Roma to runners-up in the league in 1986, will become the sixth.
Roma, currently 12th in serie A, were forced to look at other coaches after Giovanni Trapattoni said on Monday he was staying at Bayern Munich.

That declaration left Roma, who fired Argentine Carlos Bianchi earlier in the season and appointed Liedholm, in a difficult situation at a point when many clubs had already selected their new management teams for 1997/98.

Zeman, who is not coaching at the moment, had been written off by Italian newspapers on Tuesday in a list of possible contenders which included Fiorentina's Claudio Ranieri, a former Roma player, and Milan's Arrigo Sacchi.
"(Zeman) is out of the running...because he is from Lazio, who without him have taken off," La Gazzetta dello Sport said.

Lazio under Zoff have moved up to fifth in the league after a poor mid-table showing under the Czech. Zeman had been heavily criticised by some former players, including Juventus's Croat striker Alen Boksic, for his tough training methods at Lazio.
Before Lazio, Zeman -- who left his homeland as a 21 year old when Russian tanks moved in to Czechoslovakia -- had found success at then serie A club Foggia.
He later took over unsuccessfully from Sacchi at Parma in serie B and coached Sicilian club Messina.
